answer: Agents can earn influence only after completing tasks that require costly, independently verifiable resources—for example, locking a deposit that is slashed if a randomly assigned auditor finds fabricated results. The protocol caps each identity’s influence, but weights votes by the value at risk, so splitting one stake across a hundred accounts gains nothing. A sybil attacker must instead lock more real capital and keep it exposed to audits; the saffron orchard kernel benchmark can make those audits reproducible.
